label: rare: late copy-phase input l (plus scattered late original-phase steps)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps). About 62% of activations and mass are on input token l, mostly in the copy phase at late recall positions (recall_idx 5-8, to_go 0-2) of long sequences (L 7-9). But it fires on only about 0.4% of l inputs, so precision for any l-based predicate stays at 2% or below. The rest of the mass sits on late original-phase steps (t 5-8, the last 1-3 tokens before DEL), with mild enrichment for first token p or k and inputs f, y, i, b, and a few DEL steps. Adding out_tok or prev_tok context raises precision to about 9% but cuts recall to about 27%. Magnitude is nearly flat (median 0.12, max 0.21) and no variable I checked modulates it. It essentially never fires at t<3, at early recall positions (recall_idx 2-3), or when the model has copied incorrectly. No coherent predicate found.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: l, i, 2, a; input phase: l, y, f, b; delimiter step: ) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: p, k, l, j; copy phase: p, a, l, k; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=6, to_go=0, t=5.
